gen_risks.description: Delay or failure in developing the internal Customer Relationship Management (CRM) minimum-viable product (MVP) by November 2025 could disrupt school onboarding and support processing before the April 2026 launch.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement agile development milestones, conduct rigorous user acceptance testing prior to November 2025, and prepare manual contingency support workflows for Expression of Interest processing.
gen_risks.evidence: develop a customer relationship management system internally, working towards a minimum-viable product from November 2025.

gen_risks.description: Primary schools experiencing severe physical estate and room capacity limitations may be unable to accommodate all eligible pupils for 30 minutes of supervised breakfast provision.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy technical estate advisers to evaluate school premises, design flexible spatial usage models, and assist schools with adaptable delivery arrangements.
gen_risks.evidence: continuing contracts of technical estate advisers to test what schools can do to mitigate any space constraints.

gen_risks.description: Legislative delays or amendments to the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill could impact the statutory mandate requiring state-funded schools to offer free breakfast clubs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain close cross-departmental and parliamentary tracking, proceed with voluntary grant-funded early cohorts, and prepare statutory guidance in advance of bill enactment.
gen_risks.evidence: the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill will place a duty on state-funded schools with primary-aged children

gen_risks.description: Delays in budget confirmation or funding approval from HM Treasury could prevent timely grant distribution via section 14 grants and compromise cohort launch schedules.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage regularly with HM Treasury, submit complete accounting officer assessments, and maintain clear governance pathways to secure early financial approvals.
gen_risks.evidence: These include timely approval and budget confirmation from HM Treasury, effective collaboration with the sector partners

gen_risks.description: Lack of multi-year budget approvals beyond Year 1 could create financial uncertainty for schools, hindering long-term staffing and operational planning for breakfast clubs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop comprehensive multi-year business cases early for future spending reviews and clearly communicate future funding planning timelines to school leadership.
gen_risks.evidence: Funding for future years will be agreed separately through business cases.

gen_risks.description: Low uptake or reluctance to apply among eligible high-disadvantage primary schools (40%+ FSM Ever 6) in Cohort 1 could result in under-recruitment for the April 2026 start.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize simplified funding mechanics, conduct direct proactive outreach to high-disadvantage schools, and highlight start-up grant support (£1,000) to incentivize participation.
gen_risks.evidence: This should ease the burden and potentially increase willingness to engage and join the programme.

gen_risks.description: Delays or drop-outs during the transition of over 1,700 National School Breakfast Programme (NSBP) schools in September 2026 could cause a gap in breakfast provision after NSBP ends in July 2026.
gen_risks.mitigation: Guarantee places for all active NSBP settings, initiate early onboarding communications in spring 2026, and streamline registration to prevent gaps in provision.
gen_risks.evidence: ensure they do not have a gap in provision after the closure of the NSBP in July 2026.

gen_risks.description: Shortages of skilled staff and resources within DfE or primary schools (e.g., breakfast club supervisors and catering staff) could compromise operational quality and delivery capacity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide standardized operational and staff training frameworks, share best practice models from early adopters, and fund local authorities to assist regional recruitment efforts.
gen_risks.evidence: availability of skilled staff and resources, in both DfE and the education sector.

gen_risks.description: Operational costs at individual school settings exceeding the simplified funding model (£25 daily rate + £1 per child) could lead to school deficit risks and reduced delivery sustainability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide a £1,000 upfront start-up grant, apply area cost adjustments, and collect cost data during rollout to refine future funding formulas.
gen_risks.evidence: there will always be a level of uncertainty at an individual school level and on a day-to-day basis.

gen_risks.description: Delays or execution issues in establishing the call-centre pilot could lead to incomplete or inaccurate administrative data collection required for monitoring and policy evaluation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Fast-track commercial procurement for call-centre operations, define clear performance metrics, and integrate automated data validation routines.
gen_risks.evidence: We will also start commercial processes to begin a call-centre pilot to support data collection.

gen_risks.description: Delays in procuring specialist delivery advisers through the educational and children's social care framework could leave schools facing complex operational challenges without guidance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Accelerate framework procurement timelines and establish central DfE advisory capacity to provide immediate interim support to onboarding schools.
gen_risks.evidence: launched a procurement process to increase the number of advisers supporting schools through the educational and children's social care framework

gen_risks.description: Insufficient engagement or slow funding distribution to Local Authorities could result in inconsistent regional system support for primary schools delivering breakfast clubs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish clear grant agreements and strategic engagement forums with Local Authorities to clarify their role in supporting schools and local childcare systems.
gen_risks.evidence: we will fund local authorities to support schools and the wider system to effectively deliver free breakfast clubs.

gen_risks.description: Fluctuations or lower-than-expected daily pupil attendance could destabilize school variable revenue streams and skew national cost and benefit projections.
gen_risks.mitigation: Structure funding with a fixed £25 daily baseline alongside variable attendance payments, and provide schools with strategies to promote steady pupil participation.
gen_risks.evidence: funds based on take-up, with a set daily amount of £25 to fund fixed costs, plus £1 for every child that attends

gen_risks.description: Non-compliance by participating schools with mandatory School Food Standards could impair nutritional outcomes and trigger public or regulatory scrutiny.
gen_risks.mitigation: Issue clear guidance on compliant food options, leverage national supply channels, and embed food standards compliance monitoring into the programme evaluation plan.
gen_risks.evidence: Food provided must be in line with school food standards.

gen_risks.description: Incurring full program operational costs immediately while educational attainment benefits require at least one year to materialize could create early value-for-money concerns.
gen_risks.mitigation: Track early short-term indicators such as attendance, readiness to learn, and food insecurity reduction to demonstrate early value while long-term attainment data accrues.
gen_risks.evidence: costs are incurred upfront while attainment benefits only materialise after at least one year.

gen_risks.description: Lack of operational coordination with existing local wraparound childcare services could cause service overlap, market disruption, or parent confusion regarding before-school care options.
gen_risks.mitigation: Align policy guidance across the free breakfast club and wraparound childcare teams, encouraging joint local authority planning and clear family communications.
gen_risks.evidence: The wraparound childcare programme aims to improve the availability of before-school (as well as after-school) childcare

gen_risks.description: Relying on only one term of learning from the 750 Early Adopter schools may fail to reveal multi-season delivery challenges, operational bottlenecks, or full-year cost dynamics.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement an iterative, multi-method evaluation plan from 2026 to 2028 with regular interim reporting to continuously adapt policy and delivery models.
gen_risks.evidence: at the point of writing, this business case had one term's worth of learning.

gen_risks.description: Special schools and alternative provision settings may encounter higher per-pupil delivery costs or complex needs that exceed the specialized funding rate (£18.95 daily + £3.23/child).
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide higher targeted funding rates for special settings and maintain flexible delivery support via specialized advisers to address unique needs.
gen_risks.evidence: At special schools, the funding rate is: £1,000 start-up grant, daily amount of £18.95, £3.23 for every child who attends each day.

gt_risks.description: Lower value for money compared to the 'do minimum' option in year 1, due to the shorter funding period available for the preferred option's new cohorts of schools.
Delivery risks around staffing and food costs for schools newly onboarded to the free breakfast clubs programme.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated through early adopter (EA) scheme insights and support funding.

gt_risks.description: Uncertainty in the labour-market benefits (parental workforce participation gains) the programme is expected to deliver.
gt_risks.mitigation: Addressed through conservative assumptions in the economic modelling.
